profile.campus: Chandler, Maricopa County, Arizona (CyrusOne Phoenix-metro campus, PHX1-PHX8)
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own facility materials and an aggregator listing dedicated to this specific building, PHX5 sits at 2305-2335 South Ellis Street, Chandler, AZ 85286, part of CyrusOne's roughly 2,000,000 sq ft, eight-building Chandler campus (PHX1 through PHX8) totaling a publicly stated 169 MW of IT capacity across the whole campus; that campus-wide MW figure is not confirmed as this individual building's own capacity, so it is not asserted here as a single-building number.

Wikipedia's entry on CyrusOne states the company acquired 55.9 acres in Chandler in September 2011 for data center construction, part of its early-2010s national expansion under then-parent Cincinnati Bell before CyrusOne's own 2013 IPO; the company was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and was taken private in a roughly $15 billion deal when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired it, closing in March 2022. Chandler's electric and water utility, Salt River Project (SRP), serves this part of the Phoenix metro; Arizona data centers' water-intensive cooling systems have drawn scrutiny from local outlets including the Phoenix New Times given the state's arid climate and ongoing water-supply debates, a regional context relevant to this campus though not a site-specific consumption figure confirmed for this particular building.

Chandler's broader appeal to data center operators, alongside CyrusOne, the same submarket has drawn large campuses from other hyperscale and colocation players, stems from Arizona's relatively low natural-disaster risk profile (limited seismic activity, no hurricane exposure), business-friendly tax treatment for data center equipment under state statute, and proximity to fiber routes linking Phoenix to Los Angeles and other West Coast interconnection points, factors industry trade press has repeatedly cited in explaining the Phoenix metro's growth as a secondary US data center hub behind Northern Virginia and Texas.

reading.body:
CyrusOne PHX5 in Chandler publishes 169 MW of IT capacity, making it the largest published data center in Arizona by announced power allocation. Arizona's state total across four published facilities is 512 MW, so this campus represents 33 percent of the state's disclosed capacity. The state has 56 mapped data center facilities overall, of which only four publish power figures, so most Arizona capacity remains unquantified in public spec pages.

The campus qualifies to host financial services workloads under PCI DSS, healthcare under HIPAA, federal government systems under FISMA, and general enterprise services under SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type 2 attestations. It holds TIA-942 tier classification and Green Globes environmental certification. These certifications indicate compliance readiness for regulated and secure operations, not confirmation of current tenancy.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 169 MW of IT load translates to roughly 4,200 racks, a capacity scale relevant to large-scale model training. The facility occupies 2 million square feet of technical space. Whether this campus will matter to AI scaling depends on whether its power allocation, location in the Phoenix metropolitan grid, and available expansion on the 55.9 acres acquired by CyrusOne in 2011 align with future demand, information the operator has not published.
